newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemalans tie pink ribbons for kidnapped student.
newsitem.headline: Guatemalans tie pink ribbons for kidnapped student.

text.p: Guatemalans sickened by a rash of kidnappings that reached epidemic proportions earlier this year have posted hundreds of thousands of pink ribbons around the capital to remember a missing university student.

"We are appealing to everybody's conscience, even to the kidnapper's (conscience), if they have one, and we also want everyone to show they reject kidnapping," said Ana Maria de Klein of Anguished Mothers, one of the anti-crime groups behind the pink ribbon campaign.
The campaign, launched last weekend, took hold when friends of kidnapped university student, Beverly Sandoval, contacted anti-kidnapping groups seeking their help.
Kidnappings have fallen from a height of around three a day in April and May and police have arrested dozens of alleged kidnappers since June. But every week still sees multiple kidnappings.

Friends of 22-year-old Sandoval, who studied forestry at the Universidad del Valle in Guatemala City, have plastered the city with posters of her. They were also distributing t-shirts bearing her image. Guatemalans tied pink ribbons to their cars and to posts in city streets.

The family of Sandoval, who was kidnapped May 30, paid a ransom for her return but kidnappers then broke off contact without giving up their victim, and police had no clue of her whereabouts, said Klein.
A wave of abductions for ransom began to plague Guatemala in January. Many Guatemalans believe former and current members of the police and military run organised kidnapping gangs for profit.
